items.title: Mat Domber interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: I broadened my listening interests from strictly Pee Wee Russell and Muggsy Spanier and Eddie Condon and Wild Bill Davison

ctx.x: Yeah. From the time I was maybe eight or nine years old my father bought a radio and in those days it had a victrola attachment to it, and in those days when they sold those things they also had records that went along with it. So one of the first things that we had in our house was the “Overture of William Tell” and Benny Goodman, some of the early Benny Goodman trios and quartets and some of the big band stuff. And I started to listen to that. Then I became an Eddie Condonite. And before I was old enough to be…

and Muggsy Spanier. I mean those were the people that I grew up with as a listener. And I was always a jazz fan. All my life I collected records and that sort of thing. And then I met up with a musician by the name of Rick Fay. Rick was playing in California and I used to go out to California on business and we got to be friends and we discovered that we had a lot of musical tastes in common. And then when they opened the — and he played at the Disney park in Anaheim — and then when they opened the park in…
You never had a big business plan and here’s how we’re going to do this.
